text:
Lynn Conway was an electronics technician and later a digital system designer and computer architect. She was recruited by IBM Research in 1964 to join the team designing an advanced supercomputer for the Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) project, where she invented multiple-issue out-of-order dynamic instruction scheduling, and her work on the ACS architecture is noted as appearing to be the first "superscalar" design.
After initially withdrawing from MIT in 1959 due to gender dysphoria, Conway resumed her education at Columbia University, earning degrees in 1962 and 1963. Following her gender transition in 1968, she continued her career as a contract programmer, digital system designer, and computer architect. At Xerox PARC starting in 1973, she co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* with Ivan Sutherland and Carver Mead and founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology. Her contributions, including the invention of dimensionless, scalable design rules and the MOSIS system, were central to the Mead–Conway VLSI design methodology and the growth of the electronic design automation industry.
